questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Bang for the buck
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Bang for the buck
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'More value for money.'

Key Points

  • Given Idiom: Bang for the buck means more value for money. (पैसे का मूल्य)
    • Example: How much bang for the buck did you really think you would get from a twelve-year-old bike—at any price?
  • From the given options, the second option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Mistake Points

  • We may think from the phrase "Bang for the buck" that it is all about a vertical jump performed by a horse or a vehicle making sudden jerky movements.
     

Additional Information

  • The idiom has a political origin. The first recorded use is in 1954 during the US President Dwight D. Eisenhower’s administration, when his Defense Secretary, Charles Erwin Wilson, used this phrase as the title New Look policy of depending on nuclear weapons. Today, the idiom is used to mean more worth for the money used. “More bang for the buck” was preceded by “more bounce to the ounce,” an advertising catchphrase used in 1950 to market the carbonated soft drink Pepsi.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom. To be light years away
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom.

To be light years away

options.text: To be too distant for human beings to reach
options.html: To be too distant for human beings to reach

options.text: An unlikely event that happened suddenly
options.html: An unlikely event that happened suddenly

options.text: An extremely long time from now in the past or future
options.html: An extremely long time from now in the past or future

options.text: When something seems like it is about to happen in the near future
options.html: When something seems like it is about to happen in the near future

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To be too distant for human beings to reach.

Key Points

  • The idiom "To be light years away" means to refer to something that is extremely far away or distant, usually beyond the reach of human beings. (बहुत दूर होना)
    • Example: Technological advancements that we can only dream of now might be light years away.
  • Option 1 "To be too distant for human beings to reach" accurately captures this meaning. ( मनुष्यों के पहुंच से बहुत दूर)
    • Example: Exploring galaxies beyond our Milky Way is light years away in terms of current space travel technology.
  • Hence, we can infer that the meaning of the idiom "To be light years away" is best matched by option 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 2 An unlikely event that happened suddenly (असंभव घटना जो अचानक घटित हो गई)
    • Example: Winning the lottery is an unlikely event that happened suddenly.
  • Option 3 An extremely long time from now in the past or future (अत्यधिक लंबे समय से अब या भविष्य में)
    • Example: The extinction of dinosaurs happened light years ago.
  • Option 4 When something seems like it is about to happen in the near future (जब कुछ ऐसा होता है कि भविष्य में होने वाला है)
    • Example: The launch of the new product is about to happen in the near future.

questions.question: Select the sentence that uses the given idiom correctly. Cut corners
questions.questionHtml:
Select the sentence that uses the given idiom correctly.

Cut corners

options.text: He cut corners on his homework and got a bad grade.
options.html: He cut corners on his homework and got a bad grade.

options.text: The artist cut corners on the painting, and it ended up looking unfinished.
options.html: The artist cut corners on the painting, and it ended up looking unfinished.

options.text: I always make sure to cut corners when I'm driving to save time.
options.html: I always make sure to cut corners when I'm driving to save time.

options.text: I cut corners to finish my project on time, and my boss praised me for my hard work.
options.html: I cut corners to finish my project on time, and my boss praised me for my hard work.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'He cut corners on his homework and got a bad grade.'

Key Points

  • The sentence that uses the idiom "cut corners" correctly is: He cut corners on his homework and got a bad grade.
  • The idiom "cut corners" refers to doing something hastily or in a way that compromises quality by neglecting necessary steps or standards. In this sentence, it implies that the person didn't put in the required effort or complete the homework properly, leading to a bad grade.
    • Example sentence: "She cut corners while preparing the report, so it lacked crucial information."
  • It's possible that in the context of the idiom's meaning, the first sentence illustrates the concept of "cutting corners" more accurately by implying that the poor quality or outcome (the bad grade) resulted from not properly completing the homework.
     

Correct Answer: He cut corners on his homework and got a bad grade.

Additional Information

  • Origin:
    • ​The origin of the idiom "cut corners" possibly comes from the idea of literally cutting the corners of a shape or object to save time or resources.
    • In various tasks or activities, skipping corners, which represent essential steps or details, leads to an incomplete or inadequate result.
    • This phrase has been figuratively extended to denote doing something hastily or with less attention to quality.

Key Points

  • Dominating husbands (प्रभुत्व जमाने वाला पति): A husband who exercises control or influence over his wife in a forceful manner.

  • The word "jaundiced eye" means a view or attitude that is characterized by cynicism, skepticism, or suspicion. (संदेहपूर्ण दृष्टि)
    • Example: The committee viewed the proposal with a jaundiced eye, questioning every detail.
  • "Resentment" refers to a feeling of anger or displeasure about someone or something unfair. (नाराज़गी)
    • Example: She felt a deep resentment towards her boss for not acknowledging her hard work.
  • Hence, we can infer that "jaundiced eye" relates to skepticism or cynicism, which aligns with "resentment".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Jealousy (ईर्ष्या): A feeling of envy towards someone due to their achievements or advantages.
    • Example: Her jealousy over her friend's success caused a rift in their relationship.
  • Confidence (आत्मविश्वास): A feeling or belief that one can rely on someone or something; firm trust.
    • Example: His confidence in his abilities helped him secure the job.
  • Good will (सद्भावना): A friendly, helpful, or cooperative attitude or feeling.
    • Example: The company's good will towards its employees is evident in its generous benefits package.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'To believe wrongly that your situation is good.'

Key Points

  • Given Idiom: Living in a fool’s paradise means to believe wrongly that their situation is good when really it is not. (गलत तरीके से विश्वास करना कि किसी की स्थिति अच्छी है, जबकि वास्तव में ऐसा नहीं है)

  • From the given options, the fourth option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Mistake Points

  • We may think from the phrase "Living in a fool’s paradise" that it is all about living with a fool.
     

Additional Information

  • The phrase originated in a publication called the ‘Paston Letters‘ in the year 1462 although not in an exact manner that it is being used currently. Shakespeare then used the same phrase in his very popular work ‘Romeo and Juliet’ in the year 1592.

options.text: Be happy when a person leaves
options.html: Be happy when a person leaves

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Be happy when a person leaves.'

Key Points

  • Given Idiom: Be glad to see the back of means to be happy when someone leaves after an unpleasant experience with them. (जब कोई उनके साथ एक अप्रिय अनुभव के बाद चला जाता है तो खुश रहना)
    • Example: After staying without running water and sanitation for two weeks I am glad to see the back of this place.
  • From the given options, the fourth option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Mistake Points

  • We may think from the phrase "Be glad to see the back of" that it is all about being relieved at another’s failure.
     

Additional Information

  • When someone walks away from you, their back will be facing you. That means that the last thing you see as they leave is their back. Thus, it can be explained by saying that if you see the back of someone they are walking away from you. The back would thus be associated with the ending of something. This would explain why you would use it when talking about an unpleasant place or experience.

Key Points

  • Given Idiom: To make both ends meet means to have adequate money to survive or to live. (जीवित रहने या जीने के लिए पर्याप्त धन होना)
    • Example: We have to spend less to make both ends meet.
  • From the given options, the third option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Mistake Points

  • We may think from the phrase "To make both ends meet" that it is all about trying to bring two parties together.
     

Additional Information

  • One of the earliest examples of the idiom can be found in Thomas Fuller’s The History of the Worthies of England (1661). It is also said that it is translated from the French ''joindre les deux bouts de l’an'' which means to make both ends of the year meet. It implies that you have a stipend from the year and will need to live in such a manner that you do not use it all before the end of the year.
